description:
AURA — VISUAL CONTEXT OF A LIKE
PRIORITY: FUTURE INTELLIGENCE PROJECT
PHASE 1: FORENSIC ARCHITECTURE AUDIT ONLY

MODE: PLANNING / READ-ONLY

IMPORTANT:
DO NOT MODIFY THE REPOSITORY.
DO NOT CREATE OR DELETE FILES.
DO NOT IMPLEMENT ANYTHING.
DO NOT CHANGE CODE.
DO NOT CHANGE DATABASE SCHEMAS.
DO NOT RUN MIGRATIONS.
DO NOT COMMIT.
DO NOT PUSH.

This is a forensic architecture investigation only.

==================================================
OBJECTIVE
==================================================

Aura currently records a Like as durable positive behavioral evidence.

Eventually, Aura should also learn WHAT specifically attracted the user when they Like a video.

Conceptually:

User Likes video at 00:14.5
        ↓
Capture Like timestamp / playback position
        ↓
Capture surrounding video frames
        ↓
Analyze visual characteristics
        ↓
Map characteristics to Taste DNA
        ↓
Persist visual-context learning evidence

Potential visual signals include:

- Color / warmth
- Brightness
- Contrast
- Saturation
- Motion
- Texture
- Composition

This must be designed as a SEPARATE intelligence project.

It must NOT alter the existing Like/Favorite semantics.

==================================================
EXISTING LIKE SEMANTICS — DO NOT CHANGE
==================================================

The current intended behavior is:

Double-tap Like:
    recordLike(id)
    +
    addToFavorites(id)

Each double-tap produces exactly one cumulative positive Like event.

Example:

First double-tap:
    Favorites = true
    Like evidence = +1

Second double-tap:
    Favorites = true
    Like evidence = +2

Fifth double-tap:
    Favorites = true
    Like evidence = +5

Unfavoriting from Favorites:
    Favorites = false
    Historical Like evidence remains intact
    No negative Taste DNA degradation

The Visual Context project must NEVER:

- decrement Likes
- delete Like evidence
- turn a Like into an Unlike
- change Favorite semantics
- introduce negative evidence when visual analysis fails
- block the Like from being recorded

==================================================
PRIMARY INVESTIGATION
==================================================

Perform a targeted forensic audit of the repository to determine exactly how Visual Context of a Like could be implemented safely.

Do NOT perform a broad unrelated audit.

Investigate only the architecture necessary to answer the following questions.

--------------------------------------------------
1. LIKE EVENT PATH
--------------------------------------------------

Trace the complete call graph for recordLike(id).

Determine:

- Every current caller
- Every double-tap surface that can produce a Like
- Where recordLike() executes
- Whether recordLike() currently knows the playback position
- Whether the current MicroMomentEntity contains a timestamp
- Whether the timestamp represents event time, playback time, or both
- Whether playback position is available at the UI gesture layer
- Whether playback position is available in MediaRepository
- Whether any existing event already stores playback position

Identify the exact files/classes/functions involved.

DO NOT modify them.

--------------------------------------------------
2. MEDIA PLAYER POSITION
--------------------------------------------------

Investigate the current Media3 / ExoPlayer architecture.

Determine:

- Where the authoritative player instance exists
- How current playback position is exposed
- How MediaDetailScreen accesses playback position
- Whether Library, Discover, Collections, Favorites, or other surfaces have a meaningful playback position
- Whether double-tap Likes on static photos need to be excluded
- Whether a Like can occur before a video has produced a valid position
- Whether position can safely be captured synchronously at the Like gesture

Determine the safest architectural boundary for capturing:

    mediaId
    playbackPositionMs
    eventTimestamp

Do not implement it.

--------------------------------------------------
3. EXISTING FRAME EXTRACTION
--------------------------------------------------

Identify every existing mechanism Aura already has for extracting video frames.

Specifically investigate:

- MediaThumbnailFetcher
- MediaMetadataRetriever
- ThumbnailGenerationWorker
- Any Media3 frame extraction
- Any existing scene-analysis infrastructure
- Any existing AI vision pipeline
- Any existing image/bitmap processing utilities
- Any existing caching mechanism

Determine which existing infrastructure could potentially be reused.

Do NOT create a new frame extraction system if an appropriate existing system already exists.

--------------------------------------------------
4. EXISTING VISUAL INTELLIGENCE
--------------------------------------------------

Search specifically for existing infrastructure related to:

- color analysis
- brightness
- contrast
- saturation
- warmth
- motion
- texture
- composition
- scene metadata
- embeddings
- image analysis
- video analysis
- Taste DNA
- PersonalizationTraitMapper
- visual traits
- learned dimensions
- intelligence evidence

Determine whether any of these capabilities already exist.

For each relevant component, explain:

- What it currently does
- Whether it is reusable
- Whether it is synchronous or asynchronous
- Whether it is CPU/GPU intensive
- Whether it writes to the database
- Whether it already feeds Taste DNA

Do not modify anything.

--------------------------------------------------
5. TASTE DNA INTEGRATION
--------------------------------------------------

Trace the current Taste DNA learning architecture.

Determine:

- How positive evidence currently modifies Taste DNA
- How Favorite evidence differs from Like evidence
- How PersonalizationTraitMapper works
- How visual traits could theoretically map into existing Taste DNA dimensions
- Whether visual characteristics already have trait mappings
- Whether a new evidence category would be required

IMPORTANT:

Do NOT propose arbitrary new Taste DNA dimensions yet.

First determine whether existing dimensions can represent the visual signals.

--------------------------------------------------
6. CONCURRENCY AND RESOURCE ARCHITECTURE
--------------------------------------------------

This project will introduce additional media processing and concurrency.

Audit the existing architecture for appropriate mechanisms.

Determine whether Aura already uses:

- Kotlin coroutines
- Dispatchers.Default
- Dispatchers.IO
- WorkManager
- structured concurrency
- lifecycle-aware cancellation
- background processing queues
- bounded concurrency
- media-processing throttling
- caching
- resource cleanup

Identify the safest existing mechanism for future Visual Context processing.

IMPORTANT:

The future Visual Context pipeline must NEVER:

- block the playback UI
- delay recordLike()
- interfere with ExoPlayer
- interfere with Compare previews
- interfere with MediaStore scanning
- create unbounded background work
- create uncontrolled MediaMetadataRetriever instances
- process unlimited frames
- create uncontrolled bitmap memory usage

Do not implement any of this yet.

--------------------------------------------------
7. PERSISTENCE REQUIREMENTS
--------------------------------------------------

Determine what information would need to be persisted for this future feature.

Investigate whether existing tables/entities can support the feature or whether a new evidence model would eventually be appropriate.

Potential information includes:

- mediaId
- Like event ID
- playbackPositionMs
- event timestamp
- sampled frame timestamps
- visual characteristics
- analysis status
- analysis version
- confidence
- processing timestamp

DO NOT modify the schema.

Determine whether the existing micro_moments architecture can safely represent the initial event while a separate future visual-analysis evidence model handles deeper analysis.

--------------------------------------------------
8. PHOTOS VS VIDEOS
--------------------------------------------------

Determine the correct scope.

The proposed feature is primarily intended for:

    Like video
        ↓
    capture surrounding frames
        ↓
    analyze visual context

Determine how photos should behave.

Do not automatically expand scope.

If the existing architecture suggests a clean way to support photos later, identify it separately as future work.

--------------------------------------------------
9. TEMPORAL SAMPLING
--------------------------------------------------

Do NOT implement a sampling algorithm.

Instead investigate what information would be required to design one.

For example:

Like at:

    00:14.5

Potential future analysis window:

    before Like
        00:12.5
        00:13.5
        00:14.0

    Like moment
        00:14.5

    after Like
        00:15.0
        00:15.5
        00:16.5

Determine whether the current architecture makes this technically feasible.

Do not choose final sampling intervals unless repository evidence supports them.

--------------------------------------------------
10. FAILURE / CANCELLATION MODEL
--------------------------------------------------

Determine how a future Visual Context job should behave if:

- video is deleted
- URI becomes unavailable
- video is corrupt
- video is unsupported
- playback position is unavailable
- frame extraction fails
- analysis fails
- user leaves the screen
- app is backgrounded
- device is low on memory
- multiple Likes happen rapidly
- the same video is Liked repeatedly

The core Like event must remain valid even if every visual-analysis operation fails.

--------------------------------------------------
11. ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARY
--------------------------------------------------

Determine the smallest safe future implementation boundary.

Identify:

A. Files that would likely need modification.

B. New files/components that may eventually be appropriate.

C. Existing files that should remain untouched.

Pay particular attention to keeping this project isolated from:

- MediaStore scanning
- Compare preview architecture
- Main Media3 player architecture
- Favorites management
- RecommendationEngine core logic
- Existing Like/Favorite semantics

--------------------------------------------------
12. VERSIONING / REPROCESSING
--------------------------------------------------

Investigate whether future visual analysis needs an analysis version.

Example:

VisualAnalysisVersion = 1

If Aura later improves its visual analysis model, it should be possible to distinguish:

Version 1 analysis
from
Version 2 analysis

Determine whether the existing architecture has a suitable pattern for this.

Do not implement it.
